scope: Five missing military war resisters; actual US-authority custody, distinguish release from transfer or discharge, reconcile roster errors with contemporary reports.

agosto-trial.label: Holly Lewis, SocialistWorker.org, August 10, 2009, eyewitness report of August 5 court-martial and removal under guard.

agosto-release.label: Cindy Beringer, SocialistWorker.org, September 16, 2009, reports August 29 actual release and welcome-home gathering.

agosto-ivaw.label: Sarah Lazare, Courage to Resist, May 21, 2009; interview and IVAW/Under the Hood organizing context.

hall-letter.label: Marc A. Hall signed jail letter dated February 20, 2010, published March 4 by Courage to Resist; December 12 arrest and Article 134 charge. Body year 1010 is a typo.

hall-transfer.label: Courage to Resist February 16, 2010 report with February 19 and 27 updates; Liberty County detention, flight under guard, IVAW membership and legal defense statements.

hall-release.label: Courage to Resist, March 25 article with April 17, 2010 update and phone statement from freed Hall in Kuwait; discharge pending.

clousing-trial.label: JURIST, October 13, 2006; October 12 AWOL plea and eleven months with all but three suspended.

clousing-release.label: Courage to Resist, Sgt. Ricky Clousing released from brig, greeted as hero; December 2006 return and reception after actual confinement. Header December 20 precedes body December 23 homecoming; no exact release day selected.

wilkerson-trial.label: Ann Wright, eyewitness account of February 22, 2007 court-martial, Blood Diamonds and Blood Oil, March 6 column reproduced March 7 by Scoop.

wilkerson-release.label: Courage to Resist July 26, 2007 update: Wilkerson already free and working with IVAW. Underlying page header February 14 is not the release date.

aguayo-arrest.label: Jeff Paterson, eyewitness account, September 26, 2006, published September 27 on Indybay; actual surrender, handcuffing and custody at Fort Irwin.

aguayo-trial.label: Amnesty International urgent action AMR 51/041/2007, March 8, 2007; conscientious objection and US court-martial sentence.

aguayo-release.label: Amnesty International AMR 51/075/2007, April 19, 2007; confirms release April 18 from US military prison in Germany and credit for pretrial custody.

aguayo-mannheim.label: American Voices Abroad Military Project April 17, 2007 press release, reproduced April 18; Mannheim confinement since October 3 and March 6 conviction.

prisoner.name: Victor Agosto
prisoner.description: Victor Agosto was an Army communications specialist and Iraq veteran who publicly refused deployment to Afghanistan. He participated in Iraq Veterans Against the War and the Under the Hood GI coffeehouse community at Fort Hood.

cases.charges: Disobeying a lawful order connected with deployment to Afghanistan
cases.sentence: Sentenced August 5, 2009 to thirty days in jail, reduction in rank and loss of pay. He was taken away under guard after the hearing and served in Bell County Jail. Released August 29, 2009, before the full sentence expired. Military discharge was a separate later event.

case_research.custody_evidence: An eyewitness describes immediate removal under guard; the later report names the actual jail-release day and welcome-home gathering.

entries.custody_evidence: An eyewitness describes immediate removal under guard; the later report names the actual jail-release day and welcome-home gathering.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. The May refusal dates are not custody dates. The July hearing proposals were superseded by the actual August 5 hearing. An online exact birthday lacks sufficiently verified primary support and is withheld.

prisoner.name: Marc A. Hall
prisoner.description: Marc Hall was an Iraq veteran and Army specialist who protested the military’s stop-loss policy through a rap song. He challenged his detention and sought conscientious-objector status while his supporters organized a legal defense.

cases.charges: Communicating threats — Article 134, Uniform Code of Military Justice; allegations disputed
cases.sentence: Jailed December 12, 2009, initially in Georgia county custody. He remained at Liberty County Jail in February 2010 and was then transported under guard to continued US military confinement overseas, including Camp Arifjan, Kuwait. An April 17 update confirms he was free, with discharge pending. Exact release day and final disposition of all specifications are withheld; no conviction or completed sentence is asserted.

prisoner.aka: Marc Hall; Mark Hall; Marc Watercus

case_research.custody_evidence: His jail letter, contemporaneous Georgia detention notice and later guarded-transfer/release updates establish sustained custody under US authorities.

entries.custody_evidence: His jail letter, contemporaneous Georgia detention notice and later guarded-transfer/release updates establish sustained custody under US authorities.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. The custody continues across transfer: departure from Georgia is not falsely entered as release. US military custody in Kuwait is explicitly distinguished from US-soil custody. Article 132 in one update conflicts with Article 134 in his signed letter and the detailed charge account; Article 134 is used. The profile roster spells Mark; his own signature supports Marc A. Hall. No present custody asserted.

prisoner.name: Ricky Clousing
prisoner.description: Ricky Clousing was an Army interrogator who spoke publicly against the Iraq War after returning from deployment. He left his unit, later surrendered, and was jailed following an unauthorized-absence plea.

cases.charges: Absent without leave; plea avoided a desertion finding
cases.sentence: Sentenced October 12, 2006 to eleven months, with all but three months suspended under the plea agreement. A later support report describes actual imprisonment and his return home in December 2006. The suspended balance is excluded from time served. Exact commitment and release days are not established.

case_research.custody_evidence: Contemporary court reporting is followed by a support organization report of release after serving in a military prison.

entries.custody_evidence: Contemporary court reporting is followed by a support organization report of release after serving in a military prison.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. The release report header is December 20 but its body describes a December 23 homecoming. Homecoming is not necessarily release. Both support only December precision for the stored endpoint. Earlier surrender is not assumed to start continuous imprisonment. Formal IVAW membership not established; broad movement affiliation only.

prisoner.name: Mark Wilkerson
prisoner.description: Mark Wilkerson was an Iraq veteran who sought conscientious-objector status and refused another deployment. After serving a military prison term, he began working with Iraq Veterans Against the War.

cases.charges: Unauthorized absence and missing military movement; plea descriptions differ between reports
cases.sentence: An eyewitness reports conviction and a seven-month sentence on February 22, 2007. The support campaign confirms actual confinement at Fort Sill and reports him already free in its July 26 update. Precise entry and release days and total credited time remain unresolved; the seven-month sentence is not inserted as seven months actually served.

case_research.custody_evidence: The post-release campaign update confirms actual military-prison custody and subsequent freedom.

entries.custody_evidence: The post-release campaign update confirms actual military-prison custody and subsequent freedom.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. Ann Wright attended the trial and identifies AWOL and missing movement; the campaign page uses desertion in its plea description. No statutory conviction code is inferred. Its nearly-seven-month narrative does not match February-to-July arithmetic, so no exact duration is invented. The retrospective roster gives August release, but the dated July 26 update already describes him free. A namesake obituary is not used. Historical personal blog is not confirmed currently accessible, so website stays empty.

prisoner.name: Agustin Aguayo
prisoner.description: Agustin Aguayo was a US Army combat medic who sought release as a conscientious objector and refused a second deployment to Iraq. Amnesty International recognized him as a prisoner of conscience during his imprisonment by the US military.

cases.charges: Desertion and missing movement following refusal to redeploy to Iraq
cases.sentence: Taken into US Army custody at Fort Irwin, California on September 26, 2006. Later held in the US military prison at Mannheim, Germany, from October 3. Sentenced March 6, 2007 to eight months, with credit for pretrial detention. Amnesty confirms actual release April 18, 2007. The sentence and pretrial credit are not counted twice.

case_research.custody_evidence: An eyewitness documents arrest in California; the support group documents subsequent Mannheim custody; Amnesty independently confirms release after sustained US military confinement.

entries.custody_evidence: An eyewitness documents arrest in California; the support group documents subsequent Mannheim custody; Amnesty independently confirms release after sustained US military confinement.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. Qualifying custody is by US authorities, including a US military prison abroad; German civilian custody is not asserted. The roster August 2007 release conflicts with Amnesty’s contemporary April 18 confirmation and is not used. No full eight-month served duration is inferred. Reported age is not converted into a birthday. Formal IVAW membership is not inferred from supporter involvement.
